Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 27-Nov-2025 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  SEVENTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE EXAMINATIONS - NOVEMBER 2025  
  Deep learning [NPT_4124]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                      Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                Compare loss functions used in classification and regression tasks and explain how they influence      (5)  
  optimization behavior.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)           Evaluate how model interpretability differs between regression and classification problems in real-    (5)  
  world decision-making scenarios.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
2)                Compare the impact of shallow and deep architectures in feedforward networks. What advantages          (5)  
  does increasing the depth of the network provide?  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)           Analyze the relationship between the gradient of the loss function and the optimization of the         (5)  
  weights in a neural network during backpropagation.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
3)                Evaluate how augmentation strategies differ for image, text, and audio data, and their impact on       (5)  
  model robustness.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Evaluate"  
  
  B)           Evaluate the role of dropout as a regularization technique in neural networks. How does it impact      (5)  
  the training process and model generalization?  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Evaluate"  
  
4)                Evaluate how CNN architectures like ResNet or Inception overcome vanishing gradient and                (5)  
  computational efficiency challenges.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)           Examine how filter size, stride, and padding affect the receptive field and feature extraction in      (5)  
  CNNs.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  
  Page #1

5)                        Explain LSTMs manage cell states and gates to retain information over long sequences.              (5)  
  
  
  A)                                                            Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)                Evaluate LSTM performance in real-world applications such as speech recognition or sentiment       (5)  
  analysis compared to standard RNNs.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"
